main_body: Three-storey red-brick facade with a large flat stone-gray roof seen from above, a cream cornice, rows of framed windows and a green arched double door
top_band: Light lavender-gray speckled roof surface, rows ~2-38, with a lighter front parapet edge at rows ~36-40
evidence: Reading a middle column: the roof is a tall, textured, tile-divided gray surface (rows 2-38) with a vent and a skylight on it, so it clearly reads as a horizontal surface seen from above. A light parapet line closes it at rows 36-40. Below that, a cream cornice (rows 42-47) with a dark shadow row under it leads into the brick front face (rows 48-140). The windows have sills, lintels and darker frames, so they read as inset. The top band is not a thin rim, and the front face is clearly separate from it.

style.evidence: The brick has several tones (mortar, dark, mid and light bricks, with banding between floors). The cream trim has highlight and shadow steps. The roof is speckled and has slab seams, and the windows carry glass highlights and sill shading. Outlines are dark red-brown beside brick and dark gray-violet beside the roof, so they follow the adjacent material rather than being a uniform black. There are no large flat fills. Density is comparable to the references, though the roof has fewer tone steps than the Beodeul tile roofs.
